title: Four-Channel 4–20 mA I/O Module
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

open_decisions.decision: Whether the isolated host interface is UART or USB.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief explicitly offers both as alternatives ("an isolated UART or USB host interface") and does not pick one.

open_decisions.decision: How signals cross the isolation barrier — the isolation technology, the number of crossing channels, and their direction.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires galvanic isolation but names no technology, part, or channel budget.

open_decisions.decision: How the field side is powered across the barrier, and whether field power is derived on-board or supplied externally.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states isolation but is silent on isolated power transfer; it says nothing about where field-side rails come from.

open_decisions.decision: The isolation working/withstand voltage the barrier is designed to, and the specific creepage and clearance dimensions that follow from it.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires the spacing be "explicit" but states no voltage rating, pollution degree, or millimetre figure to derive it from.

open_decisions.decision: Whether a microcontroller or other digital controller is present, and which one.
open_decisions.why_open: Calibration storage and a host interface imply digital housekeeping, but the brief never names or requires a controller, let alone a specific device.

open_decisions.decision: The input signal chain architecture — sense-resistor value, single-ended vs differential sensing, converter type and resolution, per-channel vs multiplexed conversion.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies only that the inputs are 4–20 mA and that precision sense nodes get Kelvin routing; the chain itself is unspecified.

open_decisions.decision: The output driver architecture — DAC plus voltage-to-current stage, an integrated loop driver, sourcing vs sinking, and whether loops are module-powered or externally powered.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only the 500 ohm load target at nominal supply; it names no topology or part.

open_decisions.decision: The calibration storage medium, capacity, and the stored data format / calibration procedure.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says "Provide calibration storage" and stops there — no technology, size, or scheme.

open_decisions.decision: The accuracy, resolution, linearity, drift and temperature-coefficient targets, and the error budget that justifies them.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief calls the sense nodes "precision" but states no numeric accuracy requirement anywhere.

open_decisions.decision: Which specific faults count as "common wiring faults expected in a 24 V cabinet", and the protection strategy and component classes that cover them.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the fault class in words only — no fault list, no voltage/energy levels, no protection scheme.

open_decisions.decision: Field and host connector selection — type, pin count, pitch, wire gauge, pluggable vs fixed, and pinout.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief locates protection at the connector edge but never says what the connectors are.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, and mechanical mounting or enclosure/rail fit.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives no mechanical envelope, mounting scheme, or dimensional constraint at all.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup detail beyond the likely layer count — layer assignment, copper weights, dielectric choice, and whether any controlled impedance is needed.
open_decisions.why_open: Only a likely layer count of 4 comes from metadata; the brief says nothing about stackup or impedance.

open_decisions.decision: Status LED count, colours, placement, and what each one indicates.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "status LEDs" in the plural and specifies nothing further.

open_decisions.decision: Field-side reference topology — whether all four channels share one field ground domain, or channels are isolated from each other.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief isolates logic from field wiring but is silent on channel-to-channel relationships within the field side.

open_decisions.decision: Supply input handling — accepted input range around nominal, reverse-polarity and miswiring protection on the supply, and how on-board rails are generated.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the 24 V context but gives no supply tolerance window, no polarity requirement, and no rail list.

open_decisions.decision: Worst-case power dissipation budget and the thermal approach, particularly for the output loop drivers.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on thermal limits, ambient temperature, and enclosure conditions.

open_decisions.decision: Test, bring-up, calibration and programming access — test points, headers, and any self-test provisions.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mentions calibration storage but describes no calibration or test access mechanism.

open_decisions.decision: Environmental operating range and any standards, certification or EMC targets the module is designed against.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is simply silent on environment, standards and compliance.
